purpose: Probe whether the vendored oneDNN tree inside vllm-xpu-kernels can build Intel GPU grouped-memory/grouped-GEMM units for a future exact Qwen3.6 W8A8 MoE route replay.
quality_scope: No endpoint promotion and no quality claim. This only probes build viability for a later route-exact op.
source_worktree_note: The source tree already contains unrelated local W8A8/GDN/grouped-GEMM prototype changes. The tracked patch artifact only records the grouped-memory CMake flag addition.
build_stopped_reason: CMake configured successfully and the relevant oneDNN grouped-GEMM host/generated GPU units compiled. The full extension build then moved into hundreds of generated attention kernels, so it was stopped because it no longer answered the grouped-memory viability question.
negative_findings: Installed /opt/intel/oneapi/dnnl/2026.0 headers did not expose dnnl_memory_desc_create_with_grouped_encoding or DNNL_ARG_HINT_MAX_GROUP_SIZE on this host image.
The default full vllm-xpu-kernels build is too broad for fast oneDNN grouped-memory iteration.
next_steps: Create a narrow vendored-oneDNN build path, ideally oneDNN matmul-only or libdnnl-only, before adding a serving op.
Try ONEDNN_BUILD_GRAPH=OFF and a matmul-only primitive scope if this oneDNN tree accepts it.
Wrap one experimental grouped-memory matmul op using routecapture6 layer-9 inputs, then compare against the current 112-114 us W8A8 grouped-GEMM dispatch floor.
Gate any future endpoint use on max_abs_diff=0.0 against current xpu_fused_moe and accepted provenance sentinels.
